advances: Conditional actual weighted continuation at a given old regular singleton menu, including affine-only and sampled-concave variations. It neither produces a regular menu at every minimum nor treats positive-area supporting caps as linear.

proof:
The exact raw rays are feasible by the sampled tangent lemma; affine rays of either sign preserve affine positivity if affine variations alone are used. Positive common rescaling preserves sampled concavity. With $\dot V_z=-D_z$, differentiation gives $\dot w_z=(w_zD-D_z)/M$. Differentiating the moving volume-weighted log mean and then $\sum_z w_z(t)\ell_z(t)$ gives the displayed $m_z=\dot\ell_z/\ell_z$ and $\dot P_{\rm ar}$. The signed complete-cut paths of 5d743dac7de8813b are one example of an addable cone satisfying the radial hypotheses; the argument applies to any cone as stated.

For one proper group write $A_i(t)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}\Gamma_t(u_{ij})$, $F_i(z,X)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}[N_{ij}\cdot(z,X)-c_{ij}]$, and
$$
\alpha_i(t)=\min_{X\in K_{p_i}(t)}
 [F_i(p_i,X)-\varepsilon A_i(t)f_t(p_i,X)].
$$
On the old fiber the bracket is exactly $\varepsilon$ times the supporting tangent defect of $f(p_i,\cdot)$ at $y_i$, by the active thresholds and the continuous normal balance. It has its sole zero at $y_i$: $E^{1/d}$ is strictly concave inside the fiber by 5aeb5916857f97a9, hence so is its increasing concave power $E^{1/N}$, and a second zero on the boundary would give an interior zero by convexity of the defect. Projective energy is continuous under positive-body and mark convergence, including zero at the own boundary (the continuity argument in 32418f8d50e792af); thus new minimizers converge to the old interior mark. On a compact interior neighborhood, da49875a9737b172 gives the uniform marked energy expansion with old kernel and $\dot\Sigma=(D\Sigma-J)/M$, where $J=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^{\mathsf T}v_z\,dS$. Multiplication by the differentiable scalar $\ell_{p_i}(t)^{1/N}$ gives
$$
\dot f(Y_i)=\frac{f(Y_i)}N\left[m_{p_i}-\frac{C_i}{E_{K_{p_i}}(y_i)}+\frac DM\right],
\qquad
\dot A_i=\frac{D-J_i^{\rm cov}}{2M}.
$$
Testing the old mark for an upper bound on the minimum and using the old defect's nonnegativity at the new minimizers for the lower bound gives $\alpha_i(t)=t[-\varepsilon(\dot f(Y_i)+f(Y_i)\dot A_i)]+o(t)$. This argument uses only the sampled values of $\ell_t$ and does not differentiate a contact path.

Each fixed cap normal has a continuous strictly decreasing tail near its old threshold, since the old proper own section crosses an interior ball and a smaller ball persists. Uniform tail convergence follows from convergence of the fiber indicators in volume. Thus the nearby right inverse threshold $c_{ij}(t,q)$ exists on a common open mass interval about $Q$. Strict monotonicity, tail convergence, and $\alpha_i(t)\to0$ give a unique nearby solution $q_i(t)\to Q$ of
$$
\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}(t,q_i(t))=\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}+\alpha_i(t).
$$
The regular cap expansion proved in dc4933b776585ce0 is geometric and does not depend on the multiplier: at threshold $c_{ij}+t b$ the new raw mass is $Q-t(L_{ij}+S_{ij}b)+o(t)$ uniformly for bounded $b$. Invert by bracketing $b$ on either side of $-(L_{ij}+r)/S_{ij}$ at mass $Q+tr$ for each fixed bounded $r$. The weighted threshold sum at this mass equals $\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}-t(\sum_j\rho_{ij}L_{ij}/S_{ij}+rB_i)+o(t)$. Bracketing $r$ about $-(\dot\alpha_i+\sum_j\rho_{ij}L_{ij}/S_{ij})/B_i$ gives
$\dot q_i=-\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}-\dot\alpha_i/B_i$. Every current mark on that base has some through-mark threshold at least its corresponding inverse threshold, since the weighted through-mark sum is at least the right side of the inverse equation. Its depth is therefore at most $q_i(t)$. For an assigned atomic cap, the raw budget is its actual moving captured mass, with derivative $-\sum_{z\in G_s\cap P}D_z$.

If any off-$I$ gaps failed uniformly, a sequence of current marks at one such base would tend to an old mark of depth below $Q$. Select one fixed old normal with strict gap at that limit. Its through-mark thresholds and captured volumes converge by the continuity of the buffer and the zero volume of each nonvertical cut plane; for a pure-base cap membership of the sampled bases is fixed. This contradicts failure of the gap. The proper and atomic budgets tend to $Q$, so they cover the actual maximum for small $t$. Divide by $M_t$ and add the same arithmetic penalty to each budget. This gives the stated $R_i,R_s$ with all volume and covariance terms on the same path.

At a genuine local minimum, no response vector can have all entries strictly positive. These response vectors form a convex cone by addability, the regular fixed-cap shell formula, and linearity in $h$. Separation from the open positive orthant gives a nonzero nonnegative functional nonpositive on the cone, normalized to $\eta$. At $v=0$, multiply its inequality by $-N$ and collect $h$ to get the stated measures. If both signs of $h$ are allowed the inequality is equality. In the full tangent case the two $\ell$ moments equal $\Delta+NM\lambda P_{\rm ar}$, and a positive value makes $\nu$ positive on every base. Divide by this common moment, take the normalized source weights to be the masses of $\ell\mu$ and the normalized target weights to be the masses of $\ell\nu$, and apply the tight-row absorption construction in the proof of b9e0b3b29694badd to the already specified tangent inequality. Scaling back gives the claimed martingale for the same $\eta$.

statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Take a finite lattice-complete set of bases $P$ with compatible positive convex fibers $K_z$, volumes $V_z$, total volume $M$, weights $w_z=V_z/M$, within-fiber covariance $\Sigma$ and its norm $\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u}$. Let $\ell$ be positive sampled-concave with $\sum_z w_z\log\ell_z=0$ and set $P_{\rm ar}=\sum_z w_z\ell_z$. Use the cap buffer $\varepsilon f(z,x)\Gamma(u)$, with $f(z,x)=(\ell_z E_{K_z}(x)/M)^{1/N}$ for ordinary projective energy extended by zero at the own boundary, retaining ordinary pure-base caps. Write $Q$ for maximal raw depth, $\beta=Q/M$, and $I$ for the old deepest bases.

Suppose some old deepest bases are assigned finite singleton groups: a group $i$ has a base $p_i$ and own-interior maximizing mark $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$, actual nonvertical caps with normals $N_{ij}=(a_{ij},u_{ij})$, $\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$, through-mark buffered thresholds $c_{ij}$ of raw mass $Q$, and weights $\rho_{ij}>0$ summing to one with $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=\varepsilon\nabla_x f(Y_i)$. The own traces are proper and every other old trace is proper, strictly full or empty, or supporting with zero section measure. Put $S_{ij}>0$ for their mixed coareas, $B_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}$, $\theta_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/S_{ij})/B_i$ and $\delta_i=\varepsilon f(Y_i)/B_i$. Optionally cover any remaining old deepest bases by actual fixed closed pure-base caps $G_s$ of raw mass $Q$. Assume the combined menu covers $I$.

For an actual compatible signed radial path as in da49875a9737b172, let $v_z$ be its inward speed, $D_z=\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS$, $D=\sum_z D_z$, $L_{ij}$ its regular fixed-cap loss, $C_i=\int_{\partial K_{p_i}}[1+a_i\cdot(X-y_i)]^{-N}v_{p_i}(X)\,dS$ with old energy minimizer $a_i$, and $J_i^{\rm cov}=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\sum_j\rho_{ij}[u_{ij}\cdot(X-g_z)]^2v_z(X)\,dS$ with old centroid $g_z$. Independently use a raw parameter direction $h\in T_\ell$ and geometrically renormalize on the moving bodies. For a positive affine $\ell$ in the affine-only optimization, use just affine $h$ of either sign. Set
$$
m_z=\frac{\sum_qD_q\log\ell_q}{M}+\frac{h_z}{\ell_z}-\sum_qw_q\frac{h_q}{\ell_q},\qquad
\dot P_{\rm ar}=\sum_z\frac{D_z}{M}[P_{\rm ar}(1+\log\ell_z)-\ell_z]+\sum_z w_z h_z-P_{\rm ar}\sum_z w_z h_z/\ell_z .
$$
For $\lambda\in\{0,\varepsilon^2\}$, the normalized objective $\beta+\lambda(P_{\rm ar}-1)$ has on this path actual upper-cover values continuing the old equality at every row, with first derivative $-R_i/M$ on a proper row and $-R_s/M$ on an atomic row, where
$$
\begin{aligned}
R_i&=\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}-\beta D+\delta_i\left[\frac{C_i}{N E_{K_{p_i}}(y_i)}
+\frac{J_i^{\rm cov}}{2M}-\frac{(N+2)D}{2NM}-\frac{m_{p_i}}N\right]-M\lambda\dot P_{\rm ar},\\
R_s&=\sum_{z\in G_s\cap P}D_z-\beta D-M\lambda\dot P_{\rm ar}.
\end{aligned}
$$
All bases outside $I$ retain a strict gap below these budgets. If the old family and multiplier form an actual local minimum and the paths realize an addable convex cone of body speeds, there is one nonnegative simplex vector $\eta$ on the rows with $\sum_i\eta_iR_i+\sum_s\eta_sR_s\le0$ for all combined directions. In particular put $\Delta=\sum_{i\ {\rm proper}}\eta_i\delta_i$. With $\delta_z$ now denoting point mass, the same $\eta$ tests every allowed $h$ by $\langle\mu-\nu,h\rangle\ge0$, where
$$
\mu=\sum_{i\ {\rm proper}}\frac{\eta_i\delta_i}{\ell_{p_i}}\delta_{p_i}
       +NM\lambda\sum_z w_z\delta_z,\qquad
\nu=(\Delta+NM\lambda P_{\rm ar})\sum_z\frac{w_z}{\ell_z}\delta_z .
$$
For affine-only variations this holds with equality on every affine $h$. For full sampled-concave variations and $\Delta+NM\lambda P_{\rm ar}>0$, these measures admit a base martingale with $\ell$-tight rows.
